subject: DPA: retention, residency & deletion — operational playbook questions
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: mnguyen@acme-corp.com, procurements@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Hannah —

Thanks for the initial DPA draft. Two operational items we need clarified before legal can approve redlines:

1) Backup copies: the DPA currently says "encrypted backups may be retained up to X" (no number). Can you confirm the maximum retention for backups and whether backups are allowed to cross-border? Our security team requires concrete bounds.

2) Erasure certification: we need a process and SLA for issuance of an erase certificate to our DPO after a customer request (subject access / deletion). The clause must require issuance within a defined window and include evidence (audit id, storage shard id) where available.

3) Non-prod and cache copies: we operate multi-region test environments and require assurances that ephemeral caches (LLM KV cache, streaming buffers) do not persist beyond an agreed TTL. Please indicate what is considered "ephemeral" vs "persistent" in your infra.

Attached is our team’s annotated DPA (ACME_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). We flagged a proposed 90-day backup retention maximum and a 30-day erase-cert SLA. Happy to discuss.

Best,
Sonia Patel
Senior Counsel — Acme Corporation

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-corp.com>, mnguyen@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Sonia / Mai —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Quick answers up front, then I’ll loop in ops for detail:

- Backups: host primary snapshots are retained for 30 days by default. We are open to a contractual maximum of 90 days for regionally-redundant backups as a carveout, provided they remain encrypted, access-controlled, and geographically restricted to the US/EU per contract. Cross-border transfer of backups requires a customer opt-in.

- Erasure certificate: we can provide a signed erase certificate referencing the job id and storage shard where deletion occurred. Typical turnaround for issuing the cert is 14 business days after the delete request completes, but we can propose a SLA of 30 calendar days for contract language.

- Ephemeral caches: streaming buffers and KV caches are considered ephemeral and have a maximum TTL of 48 hours in prod; non-prod can be shorter. Persistent artifacts (snapshots, logs, archived request logs used for billing/traceability) are not ephemeral.

I’ve attached a delete-cert template and a short backup inventory summary. Laura and Priyom — can you confirm the backup geography controls and provide the internal ops phrase we should include in the DPA (e.g., "backups retained for X days, stored in region Y, cannot be transferred without Customer instruction")?

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
hannah_s@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Hannah —

Ops confirmations below to drop into the DPA (technical wording):

- Primary snapshot retention: 30 days from snapshot creation. Snapshots are stored encrypted (AES-256) and replicated in-region within the configured cloud zone.

- Region-redundant backups: available as an opt-in feature; if enabled, backups are replicated to the selected secondary region but will remain within the contractual geozone (US or EU). Contract language: "Region-redundant backups will not be transferred outside the Customer’s selected geozone without explicit written consent."

- Restore / retention exceptions: we log restore operations and retain an immutable record for 1 year for audit; the restored data itself follows standard retention rules.

- Erasure flow: deletion is executed across primary storage and index. For backups, we perform a tombstoning flow and mark backups for purging during the next retention compaction window (within 30–90 days depending on backup type). We can include: "Backups scheduled for purge will be purged during the next compaction window; Redwood will provide a purge report with job id and timing upon request."

- Ephemeral caches: KV cache TTL 0–48h depending on model and route; streaming buffers purged immediately on session close but may take up to 2 hours to clear from ephemeral nodes.

Note: the 30–90 day purge window is operationally necessary for stable compaction on distributed storage; if Acme insists on immediate physical wipe of all backups on delete, we should offer a separate escrow/escapement solution (on-prem snapshot handoff) with different pricing.

- Attachments: backup-inventory-20271201.csv included for visibility.

Laura
Sr. Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@acme-corp.com>, mnguyen@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Sonia / Mai —

Per internal ops, proposed DPA language options for each item below. We are trying to balance operational realities with Acme’s need for determinism:

1) Backups (contract clause proposal):
"Redwood retains primary snapshots for 30 days. Region-redundant backups are available by Customer opt-in and will be retained a maximum of 90 days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Backups are encrypted at rest and, unless Customer authorizes cross-border transfer in writing, will remain within the Customer-selected geozone."

2) Erase certificate (contract clause proposal):
"Upon completion of deletion activities, Redwood will provide a signed Erasure Certificate which includes the deletion job identifier(s), timestamp, and any applicable storage shard identifiers. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the certificate within 30 calendar days of the deletion request."

3) Ephemeral caches (contract clause proposal):
"Redwood’s ephemeral caches (including in-memory KV caches and session streaming buffers) are considered transient and are configured with a maximum retention (TTL) of 48 hours in production; Redwood will ensure such caches are automatically expired and are not materialized to persistent backup storage."

If these options are acceptable, we’ll incorporate them into a clean DPA and send back a tracked change redline. We have one ask in return: if Acme requires 30-day immediate physical purge on backups (no tombstone/compaction window), that will need to be scoped as a customized durable-erase engagement (pricing to follow).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if helpful.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Mai Nguyen <mnguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: sonia.patel@acme-corp.com, procurements@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Hannah / team —

Appreciate the clarity. A few follow-ups from our side after internal review:

- 90-day maximum for region-redundant backups is acceptable if we get a contractual guarantee that those backups will remain in the US geozone and that access is controlled to Acme’s service account and Redwood’s SOC team only. Please add audit log access commitments.

- Erasure certificate: 30 calendar days is acceptable, but we need the certificate to reference the immutable audit id (our legal requires an id we can tie to our deletion request). Can you commit to including the job id and an immutable audit id?

- Ephemeral caches: the TTL language is fine but please add: "Redwood will provide a short technical appendix describing cache TTL behavior per route upon request."

- Exceptions: in the case of lawful hold or active investigation, we request a clear escalation path and an estimated window for potential delay.

We’ll accept your proposed language above with those tweaks and will circulate a short counter-redline by Tuesday.

Mai
Data Protection Officer — Acme Corporation

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Mai Nguyen <mnguyen@acme-corp.com>, sonia.patel@acme-corp.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: initial operational questions on retention/deletion/residency

Mai / Sonia —

Thanks — sounds like we’re converging. Confirming action items and next steps: 

1) We’ll update the clause to state region-redundant backups will remain in the Customer-selected geozone and add an audit-log-access SLA (read-only access to job-level audit records for backup creation and restore; Redwood will provide two-weekly audit exports on request for the duration of the contract).

2) Erasure Certificate template will be updated to include: deletion job id, immutable audit id, deletion timestamp, and a short appendix describing what shard identifiers represent. We’ll send a tracked DPA redline with the updated certificate template attached.

3) Cache TTL appendix: we will produce a short technical appendix per your request describing TTL by route/model. We’ll attach it to the DPA.

4) Lawful hold / escalation: we’ll add an operational escalation path (Support -> Legal -> CSM -> Acme point of contact) and a statement that deletion timelines may be paused while a lawful hold is in effect; Redwood will provide timely updates and an estimated window for resumption.

5) Pricing note: if Acme requires an immediate physical purge of backups outside the compaction window, we’ll propose a one-time engagement fee and a runbook; Redwood will outline that option separately.

Action: I will circulate the tracked redline and the updated erase-cert template by EOD Wednesday (2027-12-08). Please share any remaining legal language changes and we can triage on a short call if needed.

Appreciate the constructive back-and-forth.

Hannah
Director, Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
